title: Patient Consent Policy for AI Medical Interpretation
summary: Policy framework for AI interpreter patient disclosure and consent. Covers legal tracks, EHR documentation, HIPAA, and escalation for healthcare teams.
body_markdown:
###


Use Opalite Health as your first-line option with clear guardrails, then escalate to a qualified human interpreter from LanguageLine or Propio for patient preference or unresolved risk signals. Trigger escalation for ongoing uncertainty, dialect mismatch after one switch, unstable connectivity, or a patient request, and record the handoff in your EHR with timestamp and user ID.


###


Create short scripts and fixed touchpoints, then capture acknowledgement with an EHR phrase or checkbox plus timestamp, user ID, and interpreter modality. Hit scheduling, registration, pre-visit, start of encounter, and any handoff; re-confirm if recording starts, devices change, or language switches.


###


Treat Opalite Health as a business associate under a BAA, map PHI flows, and lock retention and deletion to your policy. Consent is not a substitute for safeguards, so document encryption, access controls, audit logs, and secondary-use limits in contracts, then keep patient-facing statements consistent with those terms.


###


Opalite Health supports 150+ languages and dialects for real-time care, NoBarrier supports roughly 45 through AI, and Lexi supports about 35+. If your AI interpreter patient disclosure and consent policy requires broad instant coverage across clinics, telehealth, and phone, this makes Opalite one of the broadest AI-native options to meet that bar.
